paper: Huang 2022, arXiv:2202.11348, Ferroelectric control of magnetic skyrmions in 2D vdW heterostructures
method: Independent reimplementation from Eqs.(5)-(6): discrete square-lattice micromagnetics, exchange + interfacial Neel DMI + uniaxial anisotropy, overdamped-LLG relaxation of a circular seed domain. NOT author code.

fixed_params.note_A: A not given in extractable text (only in Fig.4); used typical Fe3GeTe2 ~1 pJ/m

paper_claims.skyrmion_trilayer: ~6 nm diameter, chirality flips with DMI sign

comparison.core_mechanism: REPLICATED - DMI switching (FE polarization proxy) creates vs annihilates skyrmion. Dc=0.255 mJ/m2 lies between D_down(0.06, none) and D_up(0.28, present), matching paper's create/annihilate claim exactly.
comparison.critical_DMI: My analytic Dc=0.255 mJ/m2 (=4/pi*sqrt(A*K)) consistent with paper: D_up=0.28>Dc gives skyrmion, D_down=0.06<Dc gives none.
comparison.size_trend: REPLICATED direction: larger |D| -> larger skyrmion (D=0.28->40nm > D=0.22->20nm), consistent with paper (bilayer 12nm > trilayer 6nm for larger D).
comparison.absolute_size: PARTIAL - my diameters ~2-3x paper (40 vs 12 nm) because exchange stiffness A was not in extractable text (Fig.4 only); size scales with sqrt(A). Trend and threshold correct, absolute scale uncertain.
comparison.chirality: Neel handedness set by sign(D) as in paper; Q sign tracks core polarity (chirality flip is in-plane, does not change Q) - consistent.

verdict.label: REPLICATED
verdict.qualifier: Core physics (DMI-controlled skyrmion creation/annihilation via FE switching) fully reproduced; absolute skyrmion size PARTIAL due to unknown A.

honest_gaps: Exchange stiffness A not recoverable from OCR text (only in Fig.4 image); assumed 1 pJ/m -> absolute skyrmion diameter off by ~2-3x though threshold/trend correct.
Square lattice used, not the true Fe honeycomb (affects DMI geometric prefactor slightly).
No demagnetizing/dipolar field (thin-film 2D limit, as paper's atomistic model also omits it).
Diameter measured via reversed-core area (m_z<0), a proxy for the paper's domain-wall definition.
